messages:
Riley: Heads up: we've seen a few customers hit weird latency spikes when their client libs switch to very large batch sizes. Proposal: add an optional client header 'x-embed-batch-hint' that signals preferred batching strategy (compact|balanced|latency). Could help router make better routing/quota choices.

Sofia M: Interesting. What values does that map to in runtime? compact = smaller per-request payload, balanced = default, latency = prefer low-latency paths even if cost higher?

Riley: Exactly. Router would map: compact -> prefer small-slot pools and avoid coalescing; latency -> route to low-p99 nodes and aggressive fastpath; balanced -> existing heuristics. Header is advisory only.

Ben K: Telemetry ops: if we accept client hints we need to surface batching efficiency in console. Right now console only shows requests/sec and average tokens/request. We should add: batch_utilization (%) and requests_coalesced/sec.

Marisol: UX ask: show per-tenant breakdown and a toggle: 'group by route' vs 'group by batch-strategy' so you can see how many customers opt into latency vs compact. Also call out when quota-exempt (dedicated) traffic isn't affected.

Sofia M: One caution: header can be spoofed. We should only honor it for SDK-authenticated requests (token prefixed with 'sdk:') or mark it as "client hint" in telemetry but enforce routing policy based on tenant entitlements.

Riley: Agreed. Honor only when (1) token flagged sdk=true OR (2) tenant has opt-in flag. Otherwise treat as metadata and include in logs for debugging.

Ben K: Storage impact: adding batch_strategy to telemetry will raise cardinality but it's small (3 values). Should be fine. The expensive bit is adding per-batch metrics: we need to emit batch_size_histogram and coalesced_count. Ops note: we already emit request_size_bytes and model_id.

Marisol: Rollout plan suggestion: feature-gate header on SDK v2.1, server honors for beta tenants only. Console: add 'Batching efficiency' card to Embeddings Route page (7d/30d) and a small alert when avg_batch_util < 30% for >15m.

Sofia M: Alert semantics: avg_batch_util = sum(payload_bytes_in_coalesced_batches)/sum(capacity_bytes_for_batches) ? Need a clear definition so customers don't misinterpret.

Riley: Proposed definition: batch_util = avg(actual_total_vector_count / allocated_batch_capacity) across 1m windows. Example: if capacity is 128 vectors and actual 32 -> utilization 25%. We'll surface both numerator/denom.

Ben K: Implementation details: router already calculates allocated_batch_capacity when coalescing. We can emit metric 'coalesce.capacity' and 'coalesce.actual_count'. Console computes util = actual_count / capacity. TSDB cost estimate: extra two gauge series per route ~ 3k series, acceptable.

Marisol: Also add a tooltip: "Low utilization may indicate clients sending many underfilled requests — consider client-side batching or choosing 'compact' hint." Keep wording non-judgmental.

Sofia M: Backpressure interaction: if tenant hints latency but we detect low utilization repeatedly (wasteful), router should throttle latency preference for that tenant temporarily to protect shared pools. Need a fair policy.

Riley: Policy idea: if avg_util < 20% for 10m and tenant traffic >1 TPS, downgrade routing preference to balanced for 5m and emit a console banner and tenant metric 'latency_pref_suppressed'.

Ben K: We'd need to ensure downgrade doesn't break SLOs for that tenant. Add a canary where suppression is initially only for non-SLA tenants, and telemetry records p99 changes.

ingest-bot: job/emit-coalesce-metrics created (job-ops-20240405-07).

Riley: Action items: Ben to prototype coalesce metrics + cost estimate, Sofia to draft header spec and auth rules, Marisol to mock console card and alert copy, I'll add a one-pager on suppression policy and a small RFC. Aim to canary with 5 beta tenants in two weeks.

console-bot: Created dashboard card draft: 'Batching efficiency', panels: util over time, coalesced requests/sec, avg batch size, suppressed latency-pref events.

Marisol: One more UX note: in route settings show 'Preferred batching mode' and allow tenants to opt-in/out of honoring client hints. Makes enterprise customers comfortable.

Sofia M: Sounds good. Also add test cases for SDK: header honored only on sdk-token + opt-in.

Riley: Great, I'll post RFC link when it's up. This should help reduce both cost surprises and mystery latency spikes.
